$Comment: Extends the jar's own Sawmill.json (RPG Stations) via the SCOPED action target {Station: Sawmill, Action: Mill}: a station is an ordered list of self-contained actions, so an extension names the ACTION it adds to rather than the whole station, and naming the station beside it pins this progression to the jar's own sawmill. That scope is the deliberate choice here: an action id is not globally unique, so a bare {Action: Mill} target would also attach this XP to any other pack's action answering to Mill. The bare form is still the right one when the target is a shared, Ref'd ActionAsset that several stations reuse and the extension is meant to reach all of them. What this extension carries: (1) PerCycleContributions, the sawmill's entire progression path (see below); (2) Bonus.Lootables, this pack's own SawmillLuckTiers table, the luck-tier ladder (see that file's own comment for the loot-side rationale). Nothing else is authored here: no Worker, no Custody. Own-asset references are authored PascalCase, matching the referenced file's own name; matching stays case-insensitive so a casing slip never breaks content. PerCycleContributions: the jar's Mill action declares no contributions of its own (RPG Stations is completely progression-agnostic by design, its shipped content declares no contributions and ships inert, the same pattern as the vanilla Affinity_* assets), so this extension owns the sawmill's progression outright rather than adding a slice on top of an existing jar award. Both entries post to the mmoskilltree:skill_xp channel (Param = skill id), forwarded verbatim on the cycle-completed event and consumed by the MMO bridge, which awards it as skill XP: WOODCUTTING at 8.0/cycle, CRAFTING at 4.0/cycle. Mill also authors its own ContributionScale (the same tool-quality ladder its Bonus rolls use), which PRE-SCALES these amounts before the cycle-completed event fires, so nothing here needs to apply a multiplier a second time: the amount on the event is always the amount to grant. To re-tune the sawmill's base XP, edit the Amounts here; to re-tune how a better tool scales it, edit the jar action's own ContributionScale. The deterministic part of output quantity is NOT touched from here: how many planks a cycle yields by default lives end to end in the jar action's own Recipe.Yield plus its Bonus rolls (its tool-ladder Floors and its chance-gated windfall roll), so this extension never re-authors that number and never multiplies it from a second file. On top of that deterministic amount, a loot Roll may still add a bounded, ADDITIVE bonus via Grants.OutputItems (N extra items of the cycle's own primary output, never a copy of the whole produced stack); SawmillLuckTiers.json's WOODCUTTING-level bonus-output Roll uses exactly that route, and stays directly comparable to (never a multiplier on) the Recipe.Yield number since both are counted in the same units. Extension Bonus rolls remain additive onto the base action's own Bonus (Lootables and Rolls both union) for genuine side rewards; SawmillLuckTiers.json proves the mechanism from the Lootables side.
